user:
Research problem: How much of the zero-shot localisation quality of MVFA (pixel AUROC and Dice on a held-out modality) is retained when its segmentation adapters are trained without pixel masks, using pseudo-masks drawn only from labelled abnormal source images (a patch is anomalous when its frozen CLIP level-4 feature is farther from every normal patch of the same dataset than the 99th percentile of normal-to-normal nearest-neighbour distances on source validation data), as masks are removed from zero, one, or all three masked source datasets?

Below are 24 candidate research ideas for this problem. Group them into 4-7 method families such that ideas in the same family share their core mechanism (not merely their goal). Give each family a short name.

[A1-g0-C1] Bounded prototype pseudo-masks with an ignore band for mask-free MVFA segmentation
Derive pseudo-masks from distances to per-image re-centred normal prototypes, train the segmentation adapters only on confident patches with a sigmoid loss, and measure how much mask-supervised localisation is recovered.

[A1-g0-C2] Superpixel-snapped pseudo-masks for mask-free training of MVFA's segmentation adapters
Refine label-restricted patch pseudo-masks by majority voting inside SLIC superpixels of the raw image before using them as Dice and Focal targets.

[A1-g0-C3] Mixing label-restricted pseudo-masks with exact synthetic-lesion masks for mask-free MVFA localisation
Train MVFA's segmentation adapters on real abnormal images with pseudo-masks plus normal images carrying synthetic lesions with exact masks, and find the mixing ratio that best recovers mask-supervised localisation.

[A1-g0-C4] DINOv2-affinity propagation of label-restricted pseudo-masks for mask-free MVFA training
Grow confident CLIP pseudo-mask seeds over a DINOv2 patch-affinity graph with a random walk, and train MVFA's segmentation adapters on the propagated masks.

[A1-g0-C5] SAM2-formed pseudo-masks from label-restricted patch prompts for mask-free MVFA localisation
Prompt SAM2 with the most anomalous label-restricted patches of each abnormal source image and train MVFA's segmentation adapters on the returned masks.

[A1-g0-C6] Graph-regularised pseudo-masks: CRF smoothing on the patch grid for mask-free MVFA training
Clean label-restricted pseudo-masks with a fully connected CRF over patches whose unary term is the NN-distance score and whose pairwise term uses CLIP feature similarity and position.

[A1-g1-o1] Boundary-ignored pseudo-mask supervision with a superpixel-consistency regulariser
Instead of refining pseudo-masks, train MVFA's segmentation adapters on raw label-restricted pseudo-masks while ignoring a band around pseudo-mask boundaries and penalising variance of the predicted map inside image superpixels.

[A1-g1-o2] Joint-bilateral upsampling of patch pseudo-masks guided by the raw image
Replace superpixel majority voting with a guided (joint-bilateral) filter that upsamples the 17x17 patch pseudo-mask score to 240 px using the raw image as the edge guide, then threshold.

[A1-g1-o3] Two-round self-training: regenerating pseudo-masks from MVFA's own adapted features
Train MVFA on label-restricted pseudo-masks from frozen CLIP features, then regenerate the pseudo-masks with the trained model's adapted segmentation features and retrain once.

[A1-g1-o4] Context-prediction residual pseudo-masks: a normal-trained masked-feature predictor localises lesions
Train a small transformer on normal source images to predict a masked patch's CLIP feature from its surrounding patches, and use the prediction residual on abnormal images as a context-aware pseudo-mask for MVFA's segmentation branch.

[A1-g1-o5] DINOv2-propagated pseudo-masks tuned on synthetic lesions and mixed with exact synthetic masks
Propagate label-restricted seeds over DINOv2 affinities, tune the propagation on synthetic lesions with known masks, and train MVFA on a mixture of propagated real pseudo-masks and exact synthetic masks.

[A1-g1-o6] Detection-branch veto: MVFA's image-label-trained detection maps filter pseudo-masks for the segmentation branch
Use MVFA's own detection branch, which is trained with reliable image-level labels on all six source datasets, to keep only those pseudo-mask patches that the detection branch also considers anomalous, and train the segmentation branch on the agreed patches.

[A1-g2-o1] Size-constrained training of MVFA's segmentation branch from image-level labels
Train the segmentation adapters with image-level labels and an inequality constraint on the predicted anomalous area of each image (zero for normal images, within a dataset-specific range for abnormal ones), without pixel-wise pseudo-masks.

[A1-g2-o2] Shift-ensemble pseudo-masks: sub-patch grid jitter doubles the effective resolution of MVFA's pseudo-masks
Compute label-restricted pseudo-mask scores on four copies of each abnormal image shifted by half a patch (0 or 7 pixels in x and y), realign and average them, so the effective pseudo-mask resolution becomes 7 pixels instead of 14.

[A1-g2-o3] Agreement-gated edge-aware pseudo-masks: guided-filter scores voted in superpixels, disagreements ignored
Refine continuous patch pseudo-mask scores with a guided filter, vote them within SLIC superpixels, label pixels where both refinements agree, and ignore pixels where they disagree when training MVFA's segmentation branch.

[A1-g2-o4] Mean-teacher online refinement of pseudo-masks during MVFA training
Replace the two discrete self-training rounds with continuous refinement: an exponential-moving-average copy of the segmentation adapters predicts maps on abnormal training images, and targets are updated each epoch as a confidence-weighted blend of the initial pseudo-mask and the teacher's prediction.

[A1-g2-o5] A learned pseudo-mask refiner transferred from the masked source datasets to the unmasked ones
In label-cost settings where some source datasets keep their masks, train a small refinement network that maps (image, coarse patch pseudo-mask) to the true mask on those datasets, and apply it to the datasets whose masks were removed.

[A1-g2-o6] Occlusion attribution of MVFA's detection branch as pseudo-masks for its segmentation branch
Train the detection branch on image-level labels, then mark as anomalous the patches whose replacement by their nearest normal-bank feature most reduces the detection branch's image score, and use these attribution maps as segmentation targets.

[A1-g3-o1] Cross-level persistence pseudo-masks: anomalies that persist across MVFA's four feature levels
Mark a patch as anomalous only if its nearest-neighbour distance exceeds the normal threshold at three or more of the four CLIP levels that MVFA adapts, because lesions are anomalous at several levels of abstraction while normal-but-rare patterns usually stand out at one.

[A1-g3-o2] Counterfactual normal-twin differencing: pseudo-masks from each abnormal image's most similar normal image
For every abnormal source image, retrieve the most similar normal image of the same dataset, align it, and mark as anomalous the patches whose CLIP features differ most from the aligned twin, giving pseudo-masks that compare like with like.

[A1-g3-o3] Detection-gated mean teacher: online pseudo-mask refinement accepted only where MVFA's detection branch agrees
Refine pseudo-masks online with an EMA teacher of the segmentation adapters, but accept the teacher's updates only on patches where the image-label-trained detection branch agrees, ignoring the rest.

[A1-g3-o4] Rank-based detection-to-segmentation distillation inside MVFA
Keep the idea of teaching the segmentation branch with the detection branch's patch evidence, but replace KL distillation of sharpened distributions with a pairwise ranking loss that only asks the segmentation map to order patches as the detection map does.

[A1-g3-o5] Two-round self-training with counterfactual occlusion masks from the jointly trained model
Train MVFA on initial pseudo-masks, then regenerate the masks by counterfactual occlusion attribution of the jointly trained model's detection branch and retrain once.

[A1-g3-o6] Dawid-Skene fusion of MVFA-internal pseudo-label sources with per-dataset reliabilities
Treat the nearest-neighbour rule, the detection-branch map and the zero-shot text map as three noisy annotators of each patch, and estimate each annotator's sensitivity and specificity per source dataset with the Dawid-Skene EM algorithm, constrained by image labels, to obtain posterior pseudo-masks.
